implementation_statement: The Office Manager asks the MSP to create suite accounts; the Project Manager adds staff and subcontractor users in SYS-01. implementation_statement: SYS-01 limits each subcontractor to its own project, and only the Office Manager and Owner can sign in to SYS-02. Gap: the shared drive is one folder tree readable by all 5 email users, including HR files and owners' security drawings.

The Office Manager prepares ACH batches and the Owner releases them in the bank portal. Gap: the Office Manager can also add vendors and change their bank details in SYS-02 with no second person, and the Owner releases batches without seeing which bank details changed. evidence: Bank portal user roles; SYS-02 user list

implementation_statement: The suite and SYS-01 apply the vendors' lockout after repeated failed sign-ins.
The MSP policy locks laptops and the desktop after 10 minutes. Gap: phones and tablets are not managed, and one tablet has no passcode.

There is no remote access into the office network; staff reach SaaS over the internet. The MSP's remote management agent runs on every laptop and the desktop. Gap: the company has no evidence of how the MSP protects that tool (MFA, technician list).

Office Wi-Fi uses a password with current encryption settings. Gap: the password is given to visitors and subcontractors, has not changed since 2023, and opens the same network as company computers and the printer.

Gap: the 5 company phones and 2 tablets are not in device management, so passcodes, encryption, and remote wipe are not enforced. Planned: enroll all 7 in the productivity suite's device management by 2026-10-31.

Gap: no approved list of external systems. Superintendents forward drawings, including FC-1 drawings, to personal email to print them; FC-1 change-order drawings were uploaded to the AI tool under standard terms. evidence: Interviews 2026-07-22; AI vendor terms of service

implementation_statement: The Owner posts project photos to the website and social media. Gap: no check before posting; a June 2026 post showed an FC-1 clinic corridor with a camera and badge reader in view and was removed 2026-07-24.

Gap: no security awareness training at hire or since, and payment fraud has never been covered. Planned: 30-minute annual training for the 5 email users, a payment-fraud module, and quarterly phishing simulations, starting 2026-10.
regulatory_driver: Business need (P01 R-001, R-002; not a FAR 52.204-21 requirement)

implementation_statement: The suite and SYS-01 record sign-ins and administrator actions by default. Gaps: mailbox audit events (inbox rules, forwarding) not confirmed on for every mailbox; firewall keeps 7 days of logs.

implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews logs or alerts. Planned: alerts to the Office Manager and the MSP on new forwarding or inbox rules and risky sign-ins, and a monthly 20-minute review checklist with the MSP, starting 2026-10.

implementation_statement: Gap: the backup has never been restore-tested. The MSP's first restore test is due 2026-09-30, and a tabletop of the P08 runbook is due 2026-11-30.

implementation_statement: SaaS vendors back up their own platforms. SYS-07 copies email and files daily and keeps 30 days. Gaps: one MSP administrator account without MFA can delete the backups; no restore test; SYS-01 records are never exported.
regulatory_driver: Business need (P05; not a FAR 52.204-21 requirement)

implementation_statement: The 5 email users have named suite accounts. Gaps: the shared bids mailbox; each jobsite tablet stays signed in to SYS-01 as a Superintendent and is used by carpenters and subcontractors.
The MSP's suite administrator accounts use MFA. Gaps: the backup console and firewall management logins held by the MSP use passwords only, and the 2 SYS-01 company administrators have no MFA.
Push MFA for the 5 named suite users; text-message MFA in SYS-02. Gaps: the shared bids mailbox has no MFA, and SYS-01 MFA is not enforced.
Planned: security keys for the Owner, Office Manager, and Project Manager (the payment roles) by 2026-10-31 (P01 R-001).

The suite enforces a 12-character minimum. Gaps: the bids mailbox password is known to 5 people and unchanged since 2024; the printer and plotter keep the default administrator password; staff reuse passwords because there is no password manager.
The business email compromise runbook (P08) was approved 2026-08-31. Gap: not yet tested; the first tabletop with the MSP is due 2026-11-30.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171; N23-R03 (252.204-7012(c) only if covered defense information is ever held)

implementation_statement: On counsel's advice, the FC-1 submittal finding was reported in writing to the Contracting Officer on 2026-07-29, one business day after it was found. Gap: until POL-03, staff had no rule for reporting suspected incidents.
evidence: Copy of the notice to the Contracting Officer

implementation_statement: POL-03 and the P08 runbook together form the incident response plan. Not yet tested.

implementation_statement: In POL-02 A.1 (2026-08-31) the Owner designated the Office Manager as security and compliance lead, and recorded that the Owner is the CMMC Affirming Official.

The Office Manager collects company property and tells the MSP. Gaps: no checklist or deadline; the departed Superintendent's accounts stayed active until 2026-07-21 and the office key was not returned.
evidence: Termination file for the departed Superintendent

implementation_statement: The company's first risk assessment (P01) was completed 2026-07-31 and approved 2026-08-31. It is updated every July under POL-02 A.2.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning. Planned: quarterly external and internal scans by the MSP from 2026-10, with findings tracked in the POA&M.
The Owner approves purchases. Gaps: the subcontract template lacks the substance of FAR 52.204-21 and 52.204-25; purchase orders have no Section 889 terms; the AI tool runs on click-through terms.
The SYS-01 vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed (P09). Gaps: no review of the MSP, accounting, payroll, backup, or AI vendors; the MSP contract has no incident notice term.

The firewall denies unsolicited inbound traffic and has no open ports. The company runs no publicly accessible systems (the website is hosted by a website vendor), so there is no public component to separate. Gaps: visitors share the office network with company computers and the printer; firewall logs are not reviewed.
All SaaS services and the bank portal use TLS 1.2 or higher.

SaaS vendors encrypt stored data; the MSP encrypts the 4 laptops. Gaps: the office desktop, which holds scanned drawings and the plotter queue, is not encrypted; phone and tablet encryption is not enforced.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)2. (encrypted data is not personal information)

implementation_statement: The MSP patches the operating system and common applications on the laptops and the desktop automatically (July report: 5 of 5 current). Gaps: firewall firmware is 11 months old; phones and tablets are not checked; printer firmware has never been updated.

MSP-managed antivirus with automatic updates, real-time scanning, and weekly full scans on the 4 laptops and the desktop; the suite scans attachments; phones and tablets use built-in platform protections. This meets FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(xiii)-(xv). SP 800-53 gap found in P07: alerts reach the MSP only by email during business hours.
Built-in spam and malware filtering. Gaps: no DMARC record for the company domain; no external-sender banner.
Planned: retention rules in POL-04 4.9: 6 years for CMMC evidence (32 CFR 170.15(c)(2)) and security records; 3 years after completion for certified payrolls (FAR 52.222-8(a)).

Gap: submittals for cameras, recorders, network, and phone equipment were not screened, and the FC-1 recorder was found on 2026-07-28. Planned: Section 889 check in submittal review, with the actual manufacturer confirmed in writing by the subcontractor, by 2026-09-30.
